content:
The doctor phoned the nurse because she was late, fearing the morning surgery might be delayed.  

OR  

The doctor phoned the nurse because she was late; the patient’s condition had suddenly worsened and urgently required her expertise.  

OR  

The doctor phoned the nurse because she was late and asked for an update, unaware she had already arrived and was assisting another ward.  

OR  

The doctor phoned the nurse because she was late, only to discover she’d left an hour earlier—trapped in traffic without her phone.  

Each continuation builds on the initial reason for the call, introducing urgency, consequence, or a twist tied to the nurse’s lateness.
